answer: Each new agent identity must post a time-locked bond of scarce compute credits before it can bid on jobs or vote. The bond unlocks only after a random cohort of peers re-executes a sample of its recent work and attests consistency. A farm that spins up a nebula of clones therefore locks real credits for every head; when audits flag coordinated shale-like clustering of similar transcripts, the entire batch is slashed. Honest single agents recover their bond; the sable cost of capital and continuous uniqueness scales linearly with the number of fakes, making mass identity creation uneconomic.
